lessons.title: Watch everyone except the ball
lessons.objective: See spacing, gravity and weak-side action in real possessions.

payload.prompt: While watching the ball handler, why is off-ball action important?

options.text: Off-ball action shows you where help is coming from and who is left open.
Off-ball action tells you what play the coach called.
Off-ball action means the offense is doing poorly.

explanation.correct: Right. Off-ball movement, screening and cutting reveal the defense's weakness before the ball moves.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Off-ball action is where the real game-changing happens: screens, cuts, and how defenders react tell you why a possession succeeds or fails.

payload.prompt: What does weak-side mean when analyzing a possession?

options.text: The side of the court away from the ball where the defense rotates or leaves shooters open.
The side of the court with the worst players.
The side where fouls happen more often.

explanation.correct: Exactly. Weak-side is where help defense leaves gaps. Smart offenses move the ball to find weak-side shooters.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. The weak-side is the opposite side of the court from the ball. Help defenders leave that side open, creating opportunities.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: Watch the weak-side forward, she is already cutting before the pass.

payload.question: What is she saying?

options.text: The forward is moving without the ball, anticipating a pass or screen to get open.
The forward is on defense.
The forward is going to foul someone.
The forward just caught the ball.

payload.translation: She is pointing out that the forward is using off-ball movement to anticipate the play and get open on the weak-side before the ball gets there.

followUps.line: That is why they are so hard to defend.
followUps.why: Recognition that unpredictable off-ball action makes defense harder.

followUps.line: Their weak-side is always open because of that.
followUps.why: A good follow-up understanding that skilled off-ball movement creates mismatches.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Watching off-ball action and weak-side movement shows you how the offense works before the ball gets there.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: The spacing was too tight, so the help collapsed on the driver.

payload.question: What happened?

options.text: The offense did not spread defenders enough, so defenders could collapse on the ball handler.
The ball handler made a mistake.
The defense was playing man-to-man.
The shooter made a three-pointer.

payload.translation: She means the shooters were not spaced far enough out, so the defense could leave their spots and help on the drive.

followUps.line: Better spacing next possession.
followUps.why: Recognition that spacing is a choice the offense makes to open lanes.

followUps.line: Or better off-ball movement to stay ready.
followUps.why: Good follow-up understanding that spacing works best with quick off-ball cuts.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Spacing forces defenders to stay home on shooters. If spacing is tight, help can collapse on the driver.

lessons.title: Named sets: horns, Spain, elevator
lessons.objective: Recognize horns, Spain pick-and-roll and elevator screens.

payload.prompt: Match the named offensive sets to how they work.

pairs.definition: Two high ball screens set near the elbows; the ball handler attacks one or the other, or pops out for a three.
A ball screen where the screener dives to the basket and the ball handler continues the pick-and-roll action.
A flexible system where players move continuously without a hard set, reacting to the defense with screens and cuts.

distractorDefinitions: A defense that only plays man-to-man.
A system where the ball handler never passes.

explanation.summary: Horns and Spain are named sets; motion offense is a principles-based system where players read and react.

payload.prompt: Match screening concepts to what they set up.

pairs.definition: A series of screens where a shooter is screened, moves, and is screened again to get open.
Four players positioned in a rectangle; two bigs on the blocks, two guards at the perimeter for flexibility.
Back-to-back screens set by two defenders for one offensive player to run around and get free.

distractorDefinitions: A defensive formation with all five players in a line.
A passing pattern used in the fast break.

explanation.summary: Elevator and stagger screens free shooters; box set is a starting formation that adapts to the defense.

payload.prompt: Tap the two spots where the screeners stand in the horns set.

scene.alt: NBA basketball court with horns set positions marked

hotspots.label: Left elbow
hotspots.feedback: Right. One screener is at the left elbow.

hotspots.label: Right elbow
hotspots.feedback: Right. The other screener is at the right elbow.

hotspots.label: Left corner
hotspots.feedback: No, corners are too far from the action in horns.

hotspots.label: Top of the key
hotspots.feedback: That is where the ball handler starts, not the screeners.

explanation.correct: Perfect. Horns has screeners at both elbows, creating options for the ball handler.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Horns has both screeners positioned at the elbows, high on the court.

payload.prompt: Tap where the Spain pick-and-roll screener goes after setting the screen.

hotspots.label: Rolls to the basket
hotspots.feedback: Right. The screener dives to the rim after the screen.

hotspots.label: Pops back out
hotspots.feedback: That is a pop, not a dive. Spain means the screener rolls hard.

hotspots.label: Exits to sideline
hotspots.feedback: Spain does not have the screener leaving the action.

hotspots.label: Slides to wing
hotspots.feedback: Spain screeners dive to the basket, not slide out.

explanation.correct: Exactly. Spain means the screener dives to the basket, keeping the roll-man action strong.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Spain pick-and-roll has the screener diving hard to the basket, not popping out.

payload.prompt: Why do teams run horns sets against zone defense?

options.text: The elbows are in the gaps of the zone where defenders are thin.
Horns only work against man-to-man.
Horns guarantee a three-pointer.

explanation.correct: Right. The elbows in horns attack the soft spots where zone defenses have gaps.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Horns targets the gaps in zone defense. The elbows are attack points zone coverage struggles to cover.

payload.prompt: What is the goal of an elevator screen?

options.text: Free a shooter with multiple back-to-back screens so he stays open as he moves.
Score a layup by dunking.
Trap the ball handler.

explanation.correct: Exactly. Elevator screens use multiple blockers to keep a shooter open as he navigates the screens.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Elevator screens are multiple back-to-back screens that keep freeing the same player as he cuts through them.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: Their motion offense is so hard to defend because everyone cuts at the right time.

payload.question: What is she saying?

options.text: The team runs a flexible, adaptive system where players read the defense and move efficiently.
The team only runs set plays.
The team passes the ball once per possession.
The players are all point guards.

payload.translation: She means the team uses motion principles where players react to the defense with timely cuts and screens, making it unpredictable.

followUps.line: Yeah, they never run the same play twice.
followUps.why: Good recognition that motion offense adapts rather than relies on hard sets.

followUps.line: That takes a lot of ball movement.
followUps.why: A good follow-up understanding that motion requires crisp passing and continuous action.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Motion offense is when players read the defense and cut/screen at the right time, not following a rigid set play.

lessons.title: Advanced pick-and-roll defense
lessons.objective: Tell apart tag, top-lock, scram and peel switches.

payload.prompt: Match pick-and-roll defense concepts to how defenders react.

pairs.definition: The screener's defender runs out hard to trap the ball handler before the pick, locking him in.
The ball-screen defender briefly touches or tags the rolling big and returns to the passer.
A sudden, scrambling switch where defenders swap assignments on the fly to recover.

distractorDefinitions: A simple man-to-man defense with no adjustments.
Fouling the ball handler to stop the play.

explanation.summary: Top-lock, tag, and scram are all aggressive pick-and-roll defenses that disrupt the ball handler or roller.

payload.prompt: What does a peel switch mean in pick-and-roll defense?

options.text: The on-ball defender peels away from his man to shadow the roller, while the big can show or switch.
A switch that happens at half court.
The ball handler peels away from the ball.

explanation.correct: Right. A peel switch is a show-and-recover where the on-ball defender can briefly help on the roller.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Peel switch means the on-ball defender shows on the roller and peels back, or a full switch happens if he can't recover.

payload.prompt: When is a late switch used in pick-and-roll defense?

options.text: After the pick is set, the defenders switch late to avoid big mismatches or create a trap.
A switch that always leads to a foul.
Switching only at the end of a possession.

explanation.correct: Exactly. Late switches are a reaction after the screen is set, used when early switches are risky.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Late switches happen after the screen is already set, as a way to prevent easy rolls or attack mismatches.

payload.prompt: What is the risk of playing top-lock defense on a pick-and-roll?

options.text: The roller can slip the screen early or the passer can kick out to an open shooter.
The team always gets fouled.
Top-lock has no risks.

explanation.correct: Right. Top-lock is aggressive but leaves the passer open. Smart offensive teams kick out when facing it.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Top-lock risks leaving the passer and kick-out shooters open if the roller slips early.

lessons.title: Gravity and the passing big
lessons.objective: Explain hub offense and why shooters bend a defense.

payload.prompt: What does gravity mean in basketball strategy?

options.text: A scorer or shooter pulls defenders toward him, leaving other teammates open.
The effect of gravity on the ball during a shot.
A fouls that pulls players together.

explanation.correct: Right. Gravity is the attention a player's scoring ability commands. It opens lanes for others.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Gravity is the basketball concept of how a dangerous scorer pulls defense toward him, freeing teammates.

payload.prompt: Why is a passing big (center who can pass) valuable to modern offense?

options.text: A big at the elbow or high post can see the whole floor and kick out to open shooters when defense helps.
Passing bigs can only score dunks.
Passing bigs are not valuable in the modern game.

explanation.correct: Exactly. A passing big at the hub of the offense sees all the cuts and kick-outs from the center.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. A passing big creates gravity and can read the defense from the middle, making him a key piece of hub offense.

payload.prompt: What is hub offense?

options.text: An offense run through a center or high-post player who receives the ball and makes reads to cutters and shooters.
An offense that only shoots three-pointers.
An offense that drives to the basket on every play.

explanation.correct: Right. Hub offense centralizes ball movement through a skilled passer in the middle, creating spacing and reads.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Hub offense puts a passing big in the middle as the decision maker, distributing to cutters and shooters.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: When he touches the ball, the whole defense collapses, so his teammates get open threes.

payload.question: What is she describing?

options.text: A player's gravity; defenders converge on him, leaving shooters unguarded.
A foul being called.
A turnover happening.
A bad pass.

payload.translation: She means the star player commands so much attention from the defense that when he catches the ball, multiple defenders move toward him, leaving his teammates wide open.

followUps.line: That is why spacing matters so much.
followUps.why: Recognition that gravity only works if shooters are spaced far apart.

followUps.line: His teammates are killers from three.
followUps.why: A good follow-up understanding that gravity is useless without shooters who can finish.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Gravity is when defenders collapse on a scorer, leaving shooters open. Works best with good spacing.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: Their passing big is running the offense from the elbow, and the defense has no idea how to stop it.

payload.question: What is making them effective?

options.text: A skilled big at the elbow can read all the cutters and kick-outs because he sees the whole floor.
The big is scoring every possession.
The defense is fouling too much.
The big only shoots threes.

payload.translation: She means the offense is running through a versatile big who has playmaking ability. From the elbow (high-post area), he can pass to cutters, kick to shooters, or score himself.

followUps.line: That is why everyone wants a shooting big now.
followUps.why: Recognition that a big who can pass AND shoot is especially dangerous.

followUps.line: The perimeter players are just moving without the ball.
followUps.why: Good follow-up understanding that hub offense needs active off-ball movement from wings.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: A passing big at the elbow runs the offense by making reads. If he can also shoot, the defense is in trouble.

payload.prompt: Should a team continue running hub offense if the passing big gets into foul trouble?

situation.narrative: The passing big has three fouls early and limits his physical play. The offense has been running through him at the elbow all season.

facts.label: Big's foul status
facts.value: Three personal fouls with lots of time left

facts.label: Offensive identity
facts.value: Entire offense built around this player's playmaking

facts.label: Backup big
facts.value: Backup is capable but not a playmaker

facts.label: Game situation
facts.value: Close game in the second half

options.label: Keep running hub through him (risk a 4th foul)
options.consequence: He fouls out and the offense collapses without its engine.
considerations: Loses your best player and best passer
Backup cannot replicate the play-making
Disrupts offensive flow too much if he fouls out

options.label: Switch to a different offense or have guards handle more
options.consequence: Keeps the star on the floor and adaptable offense keeps pace without relying on one player.
considerations: Keeps star available for the end of the game
Guards or wings can run pick-and-roll instead
Reduces foul risk while staying competitive

options.label: Bench the big and go small
options.consequence: Avoids fouling out but loses rim protection and a key scorer.
considerations: Guarantees he is available later
Small-ball opens the floor but loses rebounding
May be necessary if game is not close

payload.expertNote: Good teams adjust their offense based on foul trouble. Running the same action through a player with three fouls is risky. Smart coaches shift the load to guards or pick-and-roll.

lessons.title: Series schemes: drop vs switch vs zone
lessons.objective: Follow why a team changes coverage or goes zone as a surprise.

payload.prompt: Why might a team switch from drop coverage to switch coverage in a playoff series?

options.text: The offense is exploiting the big by hunting him in space, so switching eliminates the mismatch.
Drop defense is always better than switch.
The team ran out of plays to call.

explanation.correct: Right. Series adjustments happen when the offense finds an edge. Switching removes drop-coverage vulnerabilities.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Teams switch from drop to stop mismatch hunting when the offense exploits the big sitting back.

payload.prompt: What is a zone change-up in a playoff series?

options.text: Switching from man-to-man to zone defense to confuse an offense and change coverage looks.
Changing all five players at once.
A change-up pitch in baseball.

explanation.correct: Exactly. A zone change-up is a surprise defensive adjustment that makes the offense reset its reads.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. A zone change-up means showing zone defense when the opponent is built for man-to-man, forcing them to adjust.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: They packed the paint so tight that no one could get to the rim.

payload.question: What does she mean?

options.text: The defense crowded the inside, making it impossible to score near the basket.
The offense scored too many points.
A player got injured.
The referee made a bad call.

payload.translation: She means the defense packed multiple players into the paint (the area near the basket), making driving very difficult.

followUps.line: That is why they were shooting threes.
followUps.why: Good recognition that packing the paint forces teams to shoot from outside.

followUps.line: That only works if you can defend the three.
followUps.why: A good follow-up understanding that packing the paint is risky if the defense cannot close out on shooters.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Packing the paint means putting lots of defenders in the middle. It stops drives but opens corner threes.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: Game 4 they switched to zone, and it totally threw us off.

payload.question: Why was this an adjustment?

options.text: The team came in expecting man-to-man, so zone defense was a surprise that disrupted their reads.
Zone defense is illegal.
They fouled more in zone.
Zone defense always loses.

payload.translation: She means the other team showed zone defense when the offense was built to attack man-to-man. The adjustment caught them off guard.

followUps.line: We should have adjusted our cuts.
followUps.why: Recognition that zone requires different spacing and off-ball movement than man-to-man.

followUps.line: Playoff adjustments happen every series.
followUps.why: A good follow-up understanding that smart coaches adjust defenses series-to-series.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Zone change-ups are playoff adjustments that disrupt an offense expecting man-to-man. Offenses need to adjust back.

lessons.title: Shot creation and touch
lessons.objective: Name the footwork, fakes and touch that separate scorers.

payload.prompt: What is shot creation in basketball?

options.text: A player's ability to get open for a shot by using footwork, fakes and moves on their own, not relying on set plays.
The referee creating a shooting foul.
Making a three-pointer.

explanation.correct: Right. Shot creation is the skill to improvise and get your shot off against defense without help.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Shot creation is the ability to generate offense and get your own shot through footwork, dribbling and fakes.

payload.prompt: How is a pump fake used effectively in shot creation?

options.text: Jump into your defender to make him foul or jump, then drive or shoot off the bounce.
A pump fake always results in a made shot.
A pump fake is the same as a step-back.

explanation.correct: Exactly. A pump fake freezes the defender, then the shooter drives past or rises up over him.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. A pump fake is a head or ball fake that makes the defender jump or overcommit, creating space.

payload.prompt: Fill in shot-creation moves and touches.
payload.template: A scorer under {{pressure}} from a closeout uses an {{move}} move to get space. Touch means the {{quality}} of finish he has around the rim.

explanation.correct: Perfect. Rim pressure requires quick moves like up-and-under; touch is the soft skill of finishing layups.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Rim pressure = defenders close out hard. Up-and-under is a counter move. Touch = soft hands finishing around the rim.

payload.prompt: Match shot-creation concepts.

pairs.definition: A fake shot (pump fake) followed by a drive or euro-step under the defender's raised hands.
The softness and finesse of a player's layups, floaters and midrange shots; high-touch players make difficult finish angles.
A defender closing out hard on a shooter, forcing the shooter to have quick shot-creation moves to counter.

distractorDefinitions: The pressure of the ball in the rim.
A foul called during a shot.

explanation.summary: Up-and-under is a counter to closeouts; touch is a finishing skill; rim pressure is the close defense.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: He is the best shot creator on the team because he can get his shot off anytime.

payload.question: What does she mean?

options.text: He has the skill and footwork to score on his own without relying on teammates or plays.
He shoots more than anyone else.
He is the tallest player.
He runs every play.

payload.translation: She means this player has strong shot creation: footwork, fakes and ball-handling that let him create space and get his shot off in contested situations.

followUps.line: That is why he is so hard to defend.
followUps.why: Recognition that shot creation is a player skill that makes them dangerous in isolation.

followUps.line: He uses different moves every time.
followUps.why: Good follow-up understanding that good shot creators are unpredictable.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Shot creation is having the footwork and fakes to get your own shot off against defense without much help.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: He has such soft touch around the rim, even awkward angles go in.

payload.question: What is she complimenting?

options.text: His skill at finishing layups and floaters with a soft, controlled shot touch.
His ability to block shots.
His passing accuracy.
His rebounding.

payload.translation: She means the player has exceptional finesse and control around the rim. He can make layups and floaters from difficult angles because of his soft touch and feel for the game.

followUps.line: That is what separates the great scorers.
followUps.why: Recognition that touch and finesse are hallmarks of elite scorers.

followUps.line: Defenders cannot do much about that.
followUps.why: Good follow-up understanding that touch is a skill defenders cannot stop, only respect.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Touch is the softness and finesse of a player's layups and floaters. Great touch means making difficult finishes.

lessons.title: Diagnose a possession like a coach
lessons.objective: Explain why a possession worked or failed in one sentence.

payload.prompt: Watch this possession: ball-screen at the top, defender drops, roller gets the ball inside, help defense comes, roller makes a turnover. What went wrong?

situation.narrative: A pick-and-roll where the roller was open but could not finish the play.

facts.label: Coverage
facts.value: Defender dropped back to protect the paint

facts.label: Roller action
facts.value: Received the ball but turned it over

facts.label: Help defense
facts.value: Other defender collapsed on the roller quickly

options.label: The screener set a bad screen that blocked the roller.
options.consequence: Incorrect read of the action. The screen was fine; the roller just made a play mistake.
considerations: A weak screen would affect pass quality, not turnover risk
The roller got the ball, so the screen was effective

options.label: The roller did not execute; help came fast and the roller panicked.
options.consequence: Correct diagnosis. Quick help-side rotation forced a difficult decision on the roller.
considerations: Roller had no counter or escape move ready
Needs better spacing or a secondary option
Help came too quickly, roller did not anticipate it

options.label: Poor spacing meant no kick-out option for the roller.
options.consequence: Valid point. Without spacing, the roller has no escape when help arrives.
considerations: Spacing would have created a kick-out option
But the roller could have also thrown a better pass
Shares responsibility between spacing and execution

payload.expertNote: Possession diagnosis is about seeing the chain: screen quality, defense choice, roller execution and help timing. A turnover usually traces to poor spacing or the ball handler panicking under help.

payload.prompt: A forward gets a pass on the wing, pump-fakes and the defender jumps, then the forward misses a step-back three. What was the real issue?

situation.narrative: Good shot creation move, but the final shot was poor.

facts.label: Pump-fake result
facts.value: Defender jumped and was out of position

facts.label: Alternative
facts.value: Could have driven to the rim or kicked to corner shooter

options.label: The pump-fake was not effective.
options.consequence: Wrong. The pump-fake worked perfectly; the defender was out of position.
considerations: The defender bit on the fake and left the shooter open
The issue is what happened after, not the fake itself

options.label: He took a bad shot instead of driving or passing to the open corner.
options.consequence: Right. The pump-fake opened the floor, but the step-back three was low-quality when better options existed.
considerations: 27-foot step-back is lower quality than a rim or corner three
Good shot creation ended in poor shot selection
Needs to follow shot creation with smart decision-making

options.label: His teammates were not in the right spacing.
options.consequence: Possibly. Poor spacing could have closed off the drive or corner options.
considerations: If teammates were not spaced, the drive is tougher
But a step-back three is never the best option
Shot creation is only half the skill; decision-making matters

payload.expertNote: Great shot creation is not just getting open; it is finishing the sequence with the best available shot. A pump-fake is wasted if the next move is poor shot selection.

payload.prompt: Off-ball action: two weak-side cutters run staggered screens, one gets free and catches the ball for an open three. What made this possession work?

situation.narrative: A possession where off-ball movement resulted in an excellent shot.

facts.label: Ball handler action
facts.value: Did not hold the ball; moved it quickly

facts.label: Cutter movement
facts.value: Multiple cutters and screens forced defense to work hard

facts.label: Weak-side use
facts.value: Offense attacked the weak-side where help was not

facts.label: Spacing
facts.value: Perimeter players spaced the floor properly

options.label: The ball handler made an amazing pass.
options.consequence: Partly true. A good pass finished it, but the setup was crucial.
considerations: The pass was clean, but the cutter was already open
Off-ball movement did the heavy lifting
A bad passer could still make this work if the spacing was right

options.label: Off-ball movement and spacing created the open shot before the pass.
options.consequence: Correct. The staggered screens and weak-side attack forced the defense to break down.
considerations: The cutter was free because defense was pulled elsewhere
Spacing made it impossible for defense to help
Good off-ball execution creates easy outcomes

options.label: The defense made a mistake and left him open.
options.consequence: Unlikely. Good offense forces mistakes; this was designed to attack weak-side.
considerations: This possession was executed well by the offense
Good off-ball action often looks like defensive mistakes

payload.expertNote: Diagnose possessions by watching the ball and the off-ball play. Good teams generate easy shots through spacing and movement, not just individual talent.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: That possession worked because everyone moved at the same time.

payload.question: What is she observing?

options.text: Coordinated off-ball movement and spacing created the open shot, not individual talent.
The ball moved too slowly.
The defense fouled someone.
One player scored a lot.

payload.translation: She is recognizing that the offense succeeded because players were synchronized: cuts, screens, and passes all happened in rhythm.

followUps.line: That is what good coaching looks like.
followUps.why: Recognition that synchronized offense is a coach's system, not individual brilliance.

followUps.line: Every team should run that.
followUps.why: Good follow-up understanding that coordinated movement is a fundamental skill.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Good possessions often work because of synchronized off-ball movement and spacing, not a one-on-one burst of talent.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: That pick-and-roll failed because the roller had nowhere to go when help came.

payload.question: What is she diagnosing?

options.text: Poor spacing left the roller without a kick-out option when the defense collapsed on him.
The roller was fouled.
The screener set a bad screen.
The defense was playing zone.

payload.translation: She means the offense's spacing was poor, so when help-side defense collapsed on the roller, he had no open teammate to pass to.

followUps.line: Better spacing solves that.
followUps.why: Recognition that spacing is the cure for help-defense collapses.

followUps.line: Or a quicker pass out of the roll.
followUps.why: Good follow-up understanding that execution (quick kick-out) also matters.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: When a pick-and-roll fails because help comes, diagnose whether it was spacing, a delayed pass, or the roller panicking.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: Their defense adjusted in the second half and now that play is not working anymore.

payload.question: What is she recognizing?

options.text: The defense changed its coverage or positioning, and the offense needs to counter-adjust with new reads or spacing.
The offense is playing worse.
The referee is making different calls.
It is a different team.

payload.translation: She means the defense made an adjustment (different coverage, spacing, or positioning) that disrupts a play that worked in the first half.

followUps.line: Good coaching on both sides then.
followUps.why: Recognition that adjustments are part of basketball strategy.

followUps.line: Offense should adjust back.
followUps.why: Good follow-up understanding that it is a back-and-forth between offense and defense.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: When a good offensive play stops working mid-game, the defense has adjusted. The offense needs counter-adjustments.

payload.scenario: Your friend is saying a possession was bad, but you think it was actually a good read that just did not convert.

frames.line: I think that was a solid read, even though it did not work.
frames.notes: Start by validating the play decision, not the result.
Ask for their read instead of explaining coaching points.

frames.line: Yeah, I see where the help came from. That changes the kick-out angle next time.
frames.notes: Agree and show you are thinking about future possessions.

payload.tips: Diagnosing possessions like a coach means separating good process from bad results. Discuss reads and spacing, not just makes and misses.
